The original BERT4Rec paper already includes terminal-only masking during training to align Cloze learning with next-item recommendation; inference appends [MASK] and scores from its hidden representation. Equation 8 describes averaging negative log-likelihood over the masked targets of each sequence. Thus, adding terminal supervision alone is not a new objective-alignment idea. [Original paper, §3.6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690).

The official generator creates `dupe_factor` randomly masked examples plus one terminal-only example **per sequence window**. With `dupe_factor=10`, terminal-only examples constitute 1/11 ≈ 9.1% of generated examples; random masking can also select the terminal position. Random target count is `min(max_predictions_per_seq, max(1, round(length * masked_lm_prob)))`. Crucially, `masked_lm_prob` controls target selection, while `mask_prob` controls replacement with [MASK]; the ML-1M script sets these to 0.2 and 1.0 respectively. [Generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py), [ML-1M configuration](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run_ml-1m.sh).

The implementation pools cross-entropy across all real masked targets in a minibatch, dividing by their total count, rather than averaging sequence losses equally. Consequently, example frequency differs from target weighting: for equal-length windows with k random targets, the dedicated terminal-only target fraction is 1/(10k+1); including terminal selections in random examples gives expected terminal-target fraction (1+10k/n)/(1+10k), assuming n eligible positions. These are target-count calculations, not guaranteed gradient shares. Any intervention should specify sampling frequency, target counts, and loss reduction. [Official loss](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py#L327-L366).
